code_first.code:
authorised = false
if authorised then
    print("Access granted")
else
    print("Access denied")
endif
p: Explain the first assignment or condition that determines the output.
Explain the difference between authorised access and unauthorised access under the Computer Misuse Act 1990.
code_first.a: With authorised=false: Access denied. Changing it to true prints Access granted. The Computer Misuse Act 1990 addresses unauthorised access; a user having a password does not automatically mean they have permission for every system or file. This Boolean is only a teaching model.

original_exam_questions: Name the UK law relevant to unauthorised access to a computer. [1 mark]
Give one legal consideration when installing licensed software on many computers. [2 marks]
Whether the licence permits the number and type of installations.
Explain one principle of data protection for school pupil records. [3 marks]
Collect/use for lawful specified purpose, minimise data and keep appropriately secure.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: False authorisation means the output is Access denied.

stretch.task: Add a counter that increments for denied access.
stretch.answer: False increments counter to1; true leaves it at0.

mastery.task: Design a permissions check that allows a user to read but not necessarily write a file. Test authorised role, action and account status.
mastery.hint: Use roles/permissions, not only password knowledge.
mastery.answer: A reader requesting read -> Allowed; reader requesting write -> Denied; inactive user -> Denied regardless of role.
